items.question: Can you add AI to the web app we already have?
items.answer: Yes — that is most of this work. We start by reading your codebase and how the feature would fit, then build inside your conventions instead of bolting on a separate app. Your team reviews and owns the code.

items.question: Which model will you use?
items.answer: Whichever fits the job on quality, speed and cost, measured on your own requests. We keep the model behind a small interface, so it can be switched when a better or cheaper one arrives.

items.question: Where does our data go?
items.answer: Requests go through your servers, not straight from the browser to a model provider. We use providers that do not train on your data, or run open models in your own cloud when that matters.

items.question: How long does it take?
items.answer: It depends on the feature and on your codebase, so we do not quote a number before we have seen either. We agree the scope of a first prototype on the discovery call and estimate once we have read the code.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We can keep watching quality and cost in production and keep improving the feature against the same bar. That is our Run & improve service.

what.title: What it is
what.body: An AI system that passed its evaluations on launch day can quietly get worse — new kinds of requests, a changed document, a provider’s model update. Run & improve is an ongoing engagement: we run your evaluations on real traffic, review what fails, fix it, and show you the numbers every time.
what.note: It is the last stage of <process>how we work</process>, built on the evaluations described under <evals>Data & evaluation pipelines</evals>.

spec.measureBody: The bar we agreed before launch — quality on your test set and on sampled live traffic, cost per task, and response time — tracked over time, with every change compared before and after.

items.title: Documents that keep changing
items.body: Re-indexing, freshness checks and citation audits, so answers never quote last year’s policy.

items.title: A model provider update
items.body: When a provider ships a new model version, we run your evaluations first and switch only if it holds the bar.

items.title: Cost creeping up
items.body: Find where the spend goes, then cache, route or distil so cost per task comes back down without losing quality.

items.question: How is this different from ordinary support and maintenance?
items.answer: Ordinary support keeps software running. An AI system can keep running and still get worse. Run & improve is about quality: we measure it continuously and act on it, not only when something breaks.

items.question: Do you only run systems you built?
items.answer: No. We can take over a system another team built. We start with a review and an evaluation set, so we both know where it stands before we change anything.

items.question: Who decides what “worse” means?
items.answer: We agree it with you up front: the metrics, the test set and the thresholds. When a number moves, we look at the real cases behind it before calling it a problem.

items.question: How quickly do you respond to problems?
items.answer: We agree response times and hours with you when we set up the engagement, based on how critical the system is. They are written into the agreement, not promised on a web page.

prototype.title: Prototype
prototype.body: Within weeks you see a working demo on your real data, not a mock-up. It is rough on purpose: the point is to learn quickly where the AI is strong and where it struggles.

evaluate.title: Evaluate
evaluate.body: We measure accuracy, cost, and speed against the bar we agreed, on test cases drawn from your real work. You read the same report we do, failures included.
evaluate.get: An eval report: every test case, pass or fail, and the score against the bar.
evaluate.decide: Whether it is good enough to build, or what to fix first.

build.title: Build
build.body: Production-grade integration with your systems, with security and monitoring built in from the start. The evals come along, so every release is checked against the bar before it ships.
build.get: A production system connected to your tools, with monitoring on.
build.decide: Who can use it, what it can touch, and when it goes live.

run.title: Run & improve
run.body: We watch it in production and keep making it better: we catch drift, fix the cases it gets wrong, and switch models when a better one arrives. Each improvement is measured before it ships.
run.get: A live monitor, and a note each time an improvement ships.
run.decide: Which improvements matter most to your team.

loop.title: How you stay in the loop

privacy.lede: How CraftsAI collects, uses and protects your personal information.

informationWeCollect.title: Information we collect
informationWeCollect.intro: We collect information in the following ways:

items.detail: When you use our contact, quote, or demo forms we collect the details you provide — such as your name, email address, company, phone number, project requirements, and message — together with technical metadata (your IP address and browser user-agent) used for spam prevention and security.
If you are an active client, we process your account email, your projects, invoices we issue to you, and any messages you exchange with us through the portal.
We use passwordless login. To sign you in we process your email address and one-time login codes / magic links, and — if you choose “remember this device” — a trusted-device token.
If you opt in to browser notifications, we store a device push token so we can deliver them.
Where enabled and where you consent, we collect usage analytics such as pages visited and device type.

howWeUse.title: How we use your information
howWeUse.intro: We use the information we collect to:
items: Respond to your inquiries and provide requested services
Process and manage project quotes, contracts, and invoices
Authenticate you and secure your account and our systems
Send project updates, transactional emails, and (if opted in) push notifications
Improve our website, services, and user experience
Comply with legal obligations and protect our rights

serviceProviders.title: Service providers and data sharing
serviceProviders.intro: We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. We share data only with the service providers needed to run our business, each of which processes it on our behalf:

— our notification service delivers transactional email and login codes via [email delivery provider], and delivers browser push via Google Firebase Cloud Messaging.
— where enabled, Google Analytics helps us understand site usage.

qa.response:
CraftsAI is an AI development services firm. We design, build, and run AI systems for your business:

• AI agents & automation: agents that act inside your tools and hand off to a person when it matters
• Assistants on your data: chat and search over your documents, with cited sources
• Custom models & fine-tuning: when an off-the-shelf model isn't enough
• AI inside your product: AI features in the web and mobile apps you already have
• Data & evaluation pipelines: datasets, test suites, and evals
• AI strategy sprint: two weeks, with a working prototype at the end

Would you like to know more about any of these?

Every project is priced after we understand the workflow, the data, and the bar for good, so there's no price list. Here's how it works:

• Tell us the problem on the Get an estimate page, or book a discovery call
• A person reads it and replies within 24 hours
• You get an honest written view of what AI can do there, what it will cost, and how we'd measure it

What kind of work are you considering?

We're model-agnostic: we pick the model that fits the job, and can switch when a better one arrives. Depending on the task that means hosted frontier models, open-weight models, or a model we fine-tune for you.

Around the model we build what makes it work in production: retrieval over your data, integrations with your tools, evaluations you can read, and monitoring. Your data stays yours: private deployments, and no training on it without consent.

The Work page shows the kinds of systems we build, labelled as examples:

• Support agent: resolves routine tickets and escalates the rest with a summary
• Document intelligence: turns contracts, invoices, and forms into structured data
• Sales copilot: researches accounts, drafts outreach, keeps the CRM current
• Internal knowledge assistant: answers staff questions from policies and past tickets

Want to talk through one of these for your business?

Happy to connect you with our team:

📧 **Email:** hello@craftsai.org
💬 **WhatsApp:** tap the green button at the bottom right
📝 **Contact page:** a person reads every message and replies within 24 hours

Or use Get an estimate to describe the problem in four short steps.

It depends on the scope, so we agree the timeline with you after the first call. What's fixed is the sequence:

• Discover: map the workflow, the data, and what good looks like
• Prototype: a working demo on your real data
• Evaluate: measure accuracy, cost, and speed against the agreed bar
• Build: production integration, security, and monitoring
• Run & improve: we watch it in production and keep improving it

The AI strategy sprint is the one fixed length: two weeks.
